doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

chapter: George Shearing and becoming a manager
title: Starting as manager: Teddi King, Ahmad Jamal and Shearing's move to Capitol
summary: Levy's playing experience helps him manage; Shearing suggests a company, Teddi King is his first signing, and he gets Shearing signed to Capitol.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I would think that, you know, for managing musicians, you had a really valuable experience doing everything that they do, you know, because now you know what kind of travel they need to have, what kind of arrangements need to be made.

Yeah. It was an excellent position to be in with George Shearing because they came from England and his wife had been handling everything. And they knew nothing about what was happening as far as the business end of it in this country. So it was a valuable experience for me to be able to be in that position but at the time I felt that, well this is just a job, you know, I didn’t think any further than that, until we really got into it and George said to me, “we ought to form a company and, you know, since you’re out here why don’t you handle other people?” And other people were coming to me, to you know, to work with. So one of the first people was Teddi King, was a singer. George used her on one album I think on an MGM album she sang a couple of tracks on that album. It goes back so far I can’t—
Okay, well we won’t date you with that.

Remember it all, but anyway, that was my first person to sign up as a manager. And then I said, I was only thinking in terms of musicians anyway. I didn’t know too much about singers and I didn’t, you know that wasn’t my cup of tea was the way I felt about it at that time. So we, I did sign up people like Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, that was one of the first things. And by this time George Shearing was on Capitol Records by this time. And that’s a whole other story, how we got on that. I just walked into the office in Capitol Records in California. We happened to be out there playing and I said, “we were on MGM but they didn’t pick up our option and everything, and we’d like to sign with Capitol.” They said, “fine.” And that was how we signed. Just said okay. That was it. That was the deal. But anyway—
This is 50— has to be around ‘51. Yeah. That’s about the time.
